title: Concurrency in one screen
rememberThis: async/await is for I/O waits (module 13). Task.Run and Parallel are for CPU-bound work.
Never hold lock across Redis, HTTP, SQS, or database await.
volatile for flags; Interlocked for counters; lock for short invariants — not volatile for increment.
ReaderWriterLockSlim for rare reload + many readers; ConcurrentDictionary for per-key churn.
Cache stampede: single-flight per key plus SemaphoreSlim on database — not a global lock.
bullets: Thread pool starvation comes from blocking .Result or synchronous I/O on pool threads — watch threadpool-queue-length.
Monitor exit publishes writes; volatile alone does not atomicize compound updates.
PLINQ only pays off on large sequences with non-trivial per-element work.
Bounded Channels provide backpressure between fast ingress and slow workers.
Fixed global lock order prevents deadlocks when multiple locks are unavoidable.
